passage: Note from Mrs Bhatt, play corner, Tuesday. I watched Usha and Vijay today. Usha had planned a shop game and told Vijay every line: "No, you say Welcome, not Hello. Stand there. Not there." Each time Vijay offered an idea, Usha corrected it. After the tenth correction Vijay put the toy scale down and wandered to the block area. Usha went on saying her lines to an empty counter. Later I sat with Usha and asked what Vijay might like to add to the shop. She said she would think about it. Mrs Bhatt

qa.a: Usha had planned a shop game.

qa.q: What might Usha be feeling as she goes on saying her lines to an empty counter?
qa.a: She may feel puzzled and a little lonely, and still set on the game going her way. The note cannot say for sure, but she keeps her lines going after Vijay leaves.

qa.q: What other approach could Usha try, and why?
qa.a: Usha could ask Vijay for an idea and use it in the shop. Then Vijay would feel part of the game and want to stay.

qa.q: How might the game feel to Vijay?
qa.a: It may feel like there is no room for Vijay's own ideas, since every one was corrected. Drifting to the blocks makes sense.

grounding: A child holds the pretend game to fixed rules and the other child loses interest and leaves.
